findings.claim: The telemetry spool can lose newly appended events because flush rewrites an earlier snapshot without synchronizing with producers.
findings.trigger: A consultation or rating appends after flush reads spool.ndjson but before a successful POST causes flush to overwrite it; the stale-only clearing branch has the same race.

evidence.observation: Enqueue appends directly. Flush reads the whole file, posts a batch, then uses fs::write with the remainder derived from that snapshot. No shared lock or generation check surrounds these operations.
An event appended between the read and rewrite is absent from the retained snapshot and is overwritten without being sent.

findings.verification: Hold a local intake response after flush reads event A, append event B, return success, and assert B remains queued.
findings.remedy: Use a synchronized durable outbox with atomic batch ownership and crash recovery; coordinate append, flush, and forgetting before adding the new rating delivery paths.

reviewer_checks.note: Telemetry spool code is unchanged in this range; the plan assigns the fix to wave 2.
Spool synchronization is unchanged in this range and remains assigned to wave 2.

findings.claim: Consultation and rating telemetry transmit syntactically acceptable provider/model labels instead of restricting them to vendor and model classes.
findings.trigger: A roster provider or model contains a private but syntactically valid identifier, such as customer-acme.

evidence.observation: Both event builders pass reviewer.provider and reviewer.model through label_or. safe_label accepts arbitrary short identifiers matching its character rules rather than a closed vocabulary.
The design promises telemetry classes rather than content.
The reference specifies endpoint-host vendor classification and closed model lists, including classification for saved rating judges.

findings.verification: Serialize consultation and rating events from a ledger using private provider/model labels and assert neither raw label appears.
findings.remedy: Implement shared closed classifiers for reviewers and judges, including HTTP endpoints, unknown fallbacks, and model normalization; include this in telemetry parity rather than limiting classification work to Claude.

reviewer_checks.note: Telemetry classification code is unchanged; closed classifiers remain assigned to wave 2.
Closed telemetry classifiers are unchanged and remain assigned to wave 2.

findings.claim: A failed server deletion discards the local identity and proof needed to retry, while the CLI implies a later successful DELETE will remove the old data.
findings.trigger: forget-me has a stored complaint reference, but the intake DELETE fails or times out.

evidence.observation: After logging a DELETE error, the function still removes salt, spool.ndjson, and refs.ndjson. It does not persist a deletion retry record.
The failed-deletion message says the server drops the data on the next successful DELETE.

findings.verification: Use a scratch telemetry directory and a local server returning a DELETE failure, invoke forgetting twice, and check whether the second request can identify and authenticate deletion of the original instance.
findings.remedy: Persist a durable pending-deletion identity/proof until acknowledgment, coordinate it with producers and senders, and report partial completion accurately.

reviewer_checks.note: Forgetting and retry identity code is unchanged; the plan assigns the fix to wave 2.

findings.claim: The new strip_exe helper can panic on an unrelated Unicode process name and abort a machine-wide recovery scan.
findings.trigger: A recent process has a UTF-8 name whose byte length minus four lies inside a character, such as Linux process name 日本.

evidence.observation: strip_exe slices name[name.len() - 4..] before checking the suffix. codex_server_exclusion calls it before checking the Codex prefix, and the machine-wide scan passes recent process names into that classifier.
Linux enumeration reads /proc/<pid>/comm directly. The recovery call path does not catch a classifier panic.

evidence.reference: Read-only comparison with 4cd8d18 and pinned plugin v0.6.1 process classification
evidence.observation: The earlier Rust implementation checked the .exe suffix before slicing; the plugin removes it with a regex. Neither has this new unconditional UTF-8 boundary failure.

evidence.reference: In-memory PowerShell UTF-8 inspection of 日本
evidence.observation: The name has six UTF-8 bytes, and the proposed slice index two is inside its first character.

findings.verification: Add direct classifier and scan fixtures containing 日本 and confirm both return normally with no match or exclusion.
findings.remedy: Use a boundary-safe suffix check before slicing, such as str::get on the candidate suffix followed by an ASCII-insensitive comparison; add Unicode process-name coverage.

findings.claim: Production Windows local-zone boundary handling can choose a reset instant one hour early; the chrono-tz fixtures do not validate this production behavior.
findings.trigger: With Windows local zone W. Europe Standard Time, parse 'try again at 3:00 AM' at reference 2026-10-25T02:00:00+01:00.

evidence.observation: The adapter trusts chrono's local wall-time classification. The candidate builder retains both ambiguous offsets and selects the earliest eligible instant.
Windows boundary classification includes the exact autumn upper boundary in Ambiguous and classifies the exact spring gap start as Single with the earlier offset.

evidence.reference: .NET TimeZoneInfo checks for W. Europe Standard Time
evidence.observation: Autumn 2026-10-25 03:00 is nonambiguous with offset +01:00; spring 2026-03-29 02:00 is invalid.

evidence.reference: Production retry_after_in path compared with pinned v0.6.1 Get-WallClockCandidates and ConvertFrom-WallClock
evidence.observation: The autumn trigger selects 03:00+02:00, equal to the reference instant, instead of the plugin's 03:00+01:00 one hour later. The same boundary issue affects the dated extras: spring 02:00 uses +01 instead of the plugin's +02.

findings.verification: Run targeted Windows tests using chrono::Local for exact autumn and spring transition boundaries and compare the resulting instants with the pinned plugin.
findings.remedy: Normalize production wall-time candidates against UTC-to-local round trips or use a corrected zone implementation; filter false ambiguous candidates and recognize boundary gaps while preserving genuine repeated-hour candidates. Exercise production Local alongside IANA fixtures.

findings.claim: The new normalization can discard a genuine historical Windows local offset when chrono's UTC lookup selects a different year's rules, causing a valid reset time to be treated as a gap.
findings.trigger: Using Windows Samoa Standard Time with reference 2012-01-01T14:01:00+14:00, parse 'try again at 12:00 AM'. This requires a historical or simulated reference; no specific current or future trigger was established.

evidence.observation: Normalization rejects an offset unless the UTC lookup returns it. If every candidate is rejected, the caller advances minute by minute until it finds a supposedly valid wall time.
The Windows UTC lookup selects time-zone rules using the UTC year, which can differ from the local year used to classify the original wall time.

evidence.reference: Read-only Windows registry inspection of Samoa Standard Time/Dynamic DST and .NET TimeZoneInfo checks
evidence.observation: The 2011 record has Bias 660 and daylight bias -60; the 2012 record has Bias -780 and daylight bias -60. .NET classifies 2012-01-01 midnight as valid and unambiguous at +14:00.

evidence.reference: In-memory invocation of AST-extracted ConvertTo-ZoneTime, Get-WallClockCandidates, and Select-TimeOnlyReset from pinned plugin v0.6.1
evidence.observation: The reference implementation returned 2012-01-02T00:00:00.0000000+14:00 for the trigger.

evidence.reference: New normalization combined with chrono's Windows year selection
evidence.observation: The genuine +14 midnight candidate maps to UTC in 2011 and is rejected against the -10 rules. The alternative -10 candidate maps into 2012 and is also rejected. The artificial gap ends at 14:00; the five-minute allowance accepts that already-passed instant at reference 14:01, yielding 2012-01-01T14:00:00+14:00 instead of tomorrow's midnight.

findings.verification: Add a source-faithful synthetic Samoa year-boundary fixture and assert both the valid +14 midnight classification and the pinned plugin's next-midnight result.
findings.remedy: Correct the Windows UTC lookup used as the normalization authority for cross-year rule changes, or explicitly bound the supported historical scope and retain the counterexample as a regression fixture; blindly retaining raw candidates would reintroduce F04-2.
